title: Define CodeWiki hot-state retention cleanup
summary: Separate dogfood hot state from package source cleanup, document which `.codewiki/**`, `.tmp-worktrees`, `.pi`, and local scratch paths stay, and purge only eligible artifacts through GC with restore evidence.

goal.outcome: Repo-local dogfood state, runtime scratch, and local worktree paths have clear production semantics and only eligible artifacts are purged through CodeWiki GC policy.
acceptance: Docs/file-structure map distinguish package source from `.codewiki/**` dogfood truth, generated views, runtime/session scratch, validation/build evidence, `.pi`, `.vscode`, and `.tmp-worktrees`.
`.tmp-worktrees` remains ignored or is removed only after dirty/claim checks prove safe; no production semantics depend on it.
Post-close GC dry-run identifies eligible tracked/runtime artifacts; any purge writes restore ledger with archive commit/tree proof or records deferral/block reason.
No validation/build evidence required for open/current policy is deleted.
non_goals: Do not rewrite Git history or remove validation evidence needed for recent closes.
Do not publish or push remote changes.
verification: git worktree list --porcelain and dirty-state checks
wiki_runtime gc dry-run with archive_sha/tree_sha after close checkpoint

delta.desired: Stale-looking local/dogfood paths are either documented as intentional or safely purged through GC evidence.
delta.current: User sees `.codewiki/**`, `.tmp-worktrees`, `.pi`, `.vscode`, and generated/runtime paths as stale/deprecated because production semantics are unclear after structure decisions.
delta.closure: Task closes with clear retention docs and GC dry-run/purge evidence without unsafe deletion.
